response.message:
I've drawn an Azure chat assistant for your synthetic users. It has these parts: Entra External ID handles sign-in, an App Service app runs the chat and limits how much context it sends, Cosmos DB keeps each user's conversation separate, Azure OpenAI generates the replies, Content Safety screens the text, and a Service Bus queue passes escalations to a human reviewer. For the first local test, we'll use a scripted stand-in for the model and test sign-in tokens. That checks the flow, that users can't see each other's conversations, the context limit and the escalation routing, but it doesn't test real answer quality, the real model, permissions or whether a region is supported. All of that needs a separate test against a real Azure OpenAI deployment once you've confirmed a region and model access.

When should a conversation be escalated, and who picks it up? For example, "when the assistant isn't sure or the user asks for a person, a support agent reviews it in a queue."

proposal.title: Azure authenticated conversational assistant (first sketch)
proposal.body: Scope: authenticated chat for synthetic users with per-user conversation state, a model runtime, a bounded context window, a safety check and escalation to a person. External actions are excluded. Assumptions: the region, model, account access and quotas aren't chosen or verified yet. Managed identity is assumed between services. No native Terraform generator exists for this Azure workload yet, so engineering work is required. Local tests use a mocked model and don't prove model quality, identity and access control, or deployment.

data.label: Synthetic user (browser)
data.description: Synthetic test user chatting through a browser. This is a client reference and isn't provisioned.

data.label: Sign-in
data.description: Signs users in and issues tokens. The app validates the token and uses the user's object ID as the conversation partition key. Tenant and user flow aren't chosen yet.

data.label: Chat application
data.description: Web UI and chat orchestration. It validates tokens, loads the user's recent turns, enforces a context budget (recent turns plus a summary), calls the model, runs safety checks and decides when to escalate. It returns the reply to the user. It takes no external actions. It uses managed identity to reach downstream services.

data.label: Conversation state
data.description: Per-user conversation history, partitioned by user ID. The app only reads and writes the caller's own partition. Retention isn't decided yet.

data.label: Model runtime
data.description: Chat model deployment. The model, region, quota and access are still to be verified. Local tests use scripted mock responses instead.

data.label: Safety check
data.description: Screens user input and model output. Flagged items trigger refusal or escalation.

data.label: Escalation queue
data.description: Holds escalation tickets (conversation reference and reason) for human review, with a dead-letter queue. The escalation trigger and owner are still open.

data.label: Human reviewer
data.description: The person who handles escalated conversations. This is outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: Monitoring and audit
data.description: Traces, errors, latency, token usage and escalation events. Prompt content is excluded from logs by default.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If conversations leak between users, it's a privacy breach. This rule fails closed when identity is missing.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "authenticated conversational assistant" with "per-user conversation state".
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: only authenticated users can chat, and each user can read or continue only their own conversation history. Requests without a valid token are rejected.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without a limit, long conversations push up cost, slow responses and eventually exceed the model's limits. The token value isn't set yet.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: each model call includes only a bounded context (recent turns plus a summary) within a configurable token budget.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If the assistant gets stuck or hits a sensitive case, there needs to be a safe exit. If nobody owns the queue, escalations go unanswered.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "an escalation path. No external actions in this first test."
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: the assistant escalates qualifying conversations to a human review queue without taking any external actions. The trigger and owner are still to be confirmed.

response.message: The good news is that the design is complete. The emulation found no architecture failures: every part is connected, and sign-in, user isolation, context limits and escalation are all modelled. All 8 blockers have the same cause. The product has no generator yet for an Azure chat app with Entra, App Service, Cosmos DB, Azure OpenAI, Content Safety and Service Bus, and none of the supported contracts can produce it without shrinking the scope. Changing the diagram won't fix this. It needs product engineering work: a native Azure generator, with this artifact (e96367dc…, revision 2) as the reproducer. So I'm leaving the diagram unchanged. We can still settle the missing decisions in the meantime. Which country does the synthetic conversation data need to stay in, for example "EU only" or "no restriction for synthetic data"? That decides which Azure regions we can consider for the model and Cosmos DB.
